v1.feedback: The Riley-grid-to-botanical-cup morph is legible and the parentage is clearly preserved — you can see the interference pattern living on a cupped surface, which is a genuine morph rather than a fresh start. The cream/dark-brown palette is restrained and the olive tint at height is a nice touch. However the morph animation is very slow (90s ease-in) so on first load the piece reads as a flat grid for too long — the calyx should be readable within 2-3 seconds, so either start uMorph at 0.3+ or shorten the ramp significantly. The petal lobes could use more radial separation (increase petalShape amplitude or add a second harmonic) so the cup reads as a botanical calyx rather than a generic paraboloid with mild scalloping.

v2.feedback: The Riley-grid-to-botanical-cup morph is a genuine structural transformation — the flat interference pattern wrapping onto a parabolic cup with petal lobes is a real design move, not a variable rename. However the camera sits too far back (z=22) for a form that peaks at ~8 units tall and ~7 wide, leaving the calyx as a modest object in a large dark field; pull the camera to z~14 and raise lookAt to center the cup. The olive-rim tint is a nice botanical nod but the cream-to-sepia body reads flat — add a vein-like radial modulation in the fragment shader (e.g. sin(angle*petalCount) feeding into the dark/light mix) so the Riley interference visibly traces the petal structure rather than just tiling generically. The slow morph from 0.35→1.0 over 8 seconds means first-glance reads as a half-formed blob; start at 0.6 or shorten the ramp so the calyx silhouette is legible within 2 seconds.
